data.body: At start (and on demand) the server probes what it can do: spawn processes, run git, write .ddflow, reach the network, find companion tools. The result is a knob-overridable fact ([server].exec = auto | off | sandboxed) reported in the MCP initialize text and the brief. Each gate, act and companion declares the capability it needs; when it is missing ddflow switches that step to instruct mode (NS-run-yourself) automatically instead of recording a confusing unavailable. A cannot-run is still recorded unavailable with the reason, never passed. Builds on BL-b109b112-remote-filesystem-ind (storage and git seam) without waiting for it. CONFORMANCE (r-reuse-core, r-small-files, r-everything-configurable, D-universal-principles): OPERATOR PRINCIPLES 2026-11-01: (A) ddflow is fully usable with NO shell for the user: every command and every acceptance works through MCP and chat (AskUserQuestion for acceptance, then attest); (B) ddflow may run as a remote MCP server or in a container with no shell, so it cannot run the CLI itself: its MCP answers must then INSTRUCT the agent what to run, structured and copy-pastable, and this must ALWAYS be possible; (C) agents burn many calls discovering help and options: ddflow itself must suggest the exact next commands and parameters (CLI and MCP form) so they need not. Every number, default and severity is a knob (file, CLI, MCP, prompt, org policy lock). New MCP surface goes into existing family tools as actions (tools/list has no headroom). The agent can never approve its own request; person-only stays person-only, but its route must not be a terminal. A tool that could not run is unavailable, never passed. Research R-no-shell-audit.

chunk_findings.detail: The regression called for by B70abe055ed is a plan-lint: every record-id-shaped token in every task body must resolve. This test only runs `_CITED` over `st.items["NS-capabilities"].body`. A second item whose body is `storage seam BL-missing-seam` never enters `cited`, so `dangling` stays `[]` and the assertion passes even though `ddflow show BL-missing-seam` is still "no such item". Dropping every id from the NS-capabilities body also passes, so the lint does not lock the corrected seam citation the docstring describes.
